title: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word for Mac: easier access to the Researcher agent from the document
summary: Hold: the web search control links to a Cloud Policy overview that does not document the named setting. The setting is supported by another Microsoft page already cited in the briefing; point the control link there and include the missing navigation heading. The roadmap facts, Researcher licensing and existing availability controls are supported.

claims.claim: Researcher handles complex, multi-step research within Microsoft Copilot.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Researcher draws on the web and work files, emails, meetings and chats the user can access.
claims.quote: Researcher draws insights from both the web and your work content - including files, emails, meetings, and chats you have access to.

claims.claim: Researcher is a Microsoft-built agent.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Researcher block is under Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Researcher availability is managed by a tenant-wide block because its Edit users panel is disabled.
claims.quote: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the Edit users panel is disabled. To manage their availability, block the agent for the entire tenant by using the Block action in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The Graph block operation is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access to the Graph Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block operation requires delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.

claims.claim: User licences are managed under Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; summary; Cost and licensing; controls[1].note; Scope
claims.claim: Researcher is included for users holding a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Researcher FAQ publishes a maximum of 25 queries per user per month.
claims.quote: Are there any usage limits for Researcher agent in Microsoft 365? A maximum of 25 queries per user per month.

claims.claim: The June 2025 announcement described up to 25 combined Researcher and Analyst queries per month.
claims.quote: Researcher and Analyst are pre-pinned in the app, and any user with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license can run up to 25 combined queries per month.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Researcher query runs count toward the monthly query limit.
claims.quote: any user with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license can run up to 25 combined queries per month.

claims.claim: The web search policy can be reached through Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. Open the configuration details of the policy configuration you want to change by selecting it. On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.
claims.fix: Include the Policy configurations heading: 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot'. The overview supplies navigation; https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access supplies the setting name.

claims.where: controls[2].ui.docs; Governance controls table: row 3 Learn link
claims.claim: The linked Cloud Policy overview documents the Allow web search in Copilot control itself.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Allow web search in Copilot' in overview-cloud-policy (absent); opened manage-public-web-access, which names the policy, its options and its Researcher applicability.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].ui.docs and row 3's Admin UI Learn link to https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access. Keep overview-cloud-policy in sources for the navigation steps; it does not show the control's own part of the path.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot governs Researcher's use of web data.
claims.quote: The information about web search in this article also applies to Researcher, Analyst, and Cowork in Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: The web search policy can target users or user groups.
claims.quote: This policy allows IT admins to either turn on or turn off web search for users or user groups across the tenant they manage

claims.claim: The Allow web search in Copilot policy is available only in Cloud Policy service.
claims.quote: the Allow web search in Copilot policy, which is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator is the recommended role for Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended) | This role can manage Office apps cloud services, including policy and settings management

claims.claim: No automation is documented for the group-scoped web search control shown in this row.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Allow web search in Copilot group policy automation API TCM tenant-level'; opened graph/utcm-copilot-resources and graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources. TCM writes tenant-level OCPS policies only and fails if the setting is in any group-level policy.

claims.claim: No separate Word-specific UI or API switch for Researcher entry points is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Researcher Word per-app disable entry points Cloud Policy admin switch'; opened faq-researcher, researcher-agent, agent-actions and mac/set-preference-per-app. Results describe the tenant block or Computer Use settings, not a Word entry-point switch.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default arrival behaviour of the Word for Mac entry points is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Researcher Word Mac canvas entry points rollout default report document admin setting' and 'Researcher Word entry'; read the roadmap, researcher-agent and faq-researcher. The FAQ's core default experience statement does not specify the new Word for Mac entry points.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe the appearance of the Word entry points.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Researcher Word Mac canvas entry points rollout default report document admin setting' and 'Researcher Word entry'; opened researcher-agent and faq-researcher. Neither describes the new Word canvas UI.

claims.claim: The destination of a report started from the Word canvas is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Researcher Word Mac canvas entry points rollout default report document admin setting'; opened researcher-agent and faq-researcher. They describe Researcher reports, but not where a Word-started report is placed.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics for the Word for Mac entry points are not published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Researcher Word Mac canvas entry points rollout default report document admin setting'; read the roadmap, researcher-agent and faq-researcher. No Word for Mac rollout channel, version or enablement procedure was found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No changed data reach or other changed Researcher behaviour is documented for the new Word entry points.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Researcher Word Mac canvas entry points rollout default report document admin setting' and 'Researcher Word entry'; read researcher-agent, faq-researcher and the roadmap. Only new canvas entry points are described for this item.

claims.claim: Researcher uses Microsoft Graph, connectors and the Bing index.
claims.quote: Researcher uses Microsoft Graph, connectors, and Bing index for recent web data.

claims.claim: Researcher adheres to DLP policies and follows the same policies as Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Yes, Researcher agent adheres to DLP policies and follows the same policies as Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: At work Researcher respects the existing permissions, policies and compliance.
claims.quote: It's right inside Microsoft Copilot; at work, it respects the same permissions, policies, and compliance you already rely on.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: With web search enabled, Copilot sends generated search queries to Bing.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: A query generated from a prompt inside Word may be informed by an open document.
claims.quote: it may also be informed by data within a Microsoft 365 document under the following conditions: When a user enters a prompt into Copilot inside a Microsoft 365 application (for example, writing a prompt into Copilot in Microsoft Word while a relevant document is open).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Data Protection Addendum does not apply to generated web search queries.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum (DPA) doesn't apply to the use of generated web search queries in Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Chat, or the Bing search service.

claims.claim: The EU Data Boundary does not apply to generated search queries.
claims.quote: Also, HIPAA compliance and the EU Data Boundary don't apply to generated search queries.

claims.claim: Researcher may ask clarifying questions before producing its report.
claims.quote: Researcher agent may ask clarifying questions to guide the output and keep you involved.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The FAQ describes highly complex Researcher responses as taking 10 to 45 minutes.
claims.quote: Researcher agent responses typically range from under five minutes for simple queries. Then 10 to 45 minutes for highly complex ones.

claims.claim: Users cannot disable Researcher.
claims.quote: Users can't disable Researcher agent.

claims.claim: Users cannot independently remove or unpin Researcher.
claims.quote: Researcher agent is a core part of the Microsoft Copilot experience and users cannot independently remove or unpin it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The FAQ states that Researcher session content is not directly accessible to administrators or compliance tools by default.
claims.quote: By default, no. The content of Researcher sessions isn't directly accessible to admins or compliance tools.

claims.claim: Researcher remains available under Tools in Copilot Chat when Copilot agents are disabled for some or all users.
claims.quote: This tool will remain accessible in Microsoft Copilot Chat under Tools, even when Copilot agents are disabled for some or all users in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: For this commercial-cloud scope, unconfigured Allow web search in Copilot leaves web search available unless optional connected experiences are Disabled.
claims.quote: If the IT admin doesn't configure the Allow web search in Copilot policy, web search will be available to users in both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat, unless the IT admin has set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Disabled.

claims.claim: Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat disables web search in Researcher.
claims.quote: If the IT admin chooses the Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat option, web search in Researcher and Cowork in Microsoft Copilot will be disabled.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings take effect when the Office app is restarted.
claims.quote: Policies from Cloud Policy are applied only when the Office app is restarted.

claims.claim: The Researcher FAQ and June 2025 announcement name no separate Researcher meter or charge.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Researcher agent Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing meter credits pay as you go queries'; read faq-researcher and the June 2025 announcement. Opened pay-as-you-go-meters; it does not name a separate meter for the included Researcher experience.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No licensing or charging rule specific to the Word for Mac entry points is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Researcher agent Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing meter credits pay as you go queries' and 'Researcher Word Mac canvas entry points rollout default report document admin setting'; read faq-researcher, researcher-agent, pay-as-you-go-meters and the June 2025 announcement.

claims.claim: The FAQ says there is no existing reporting tool for Researcher and Analyst.
claims.quote: No. There is no existing reporting tool for Copilot agents like Researcher and Analyst.

claims.claim: The FAQ also says administrators can see Researcher usage metrics.
claims.quote: Admins can see usage metrics (like how many times it's used) but not the actual conversation content.

claims.claim: The Researcher FAQ answers sovereign-cloud availability with To be released soon.
claims.quote: Is Researcher agent available in Sovereign Clouds? To be released soon.

claims.claim: Cost is rated none for the new entry points into Researcher already included for Copilot licence holders.
claims.quote: Now, these powerful agents are available to everyone with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
